meta.title: Generic Operator — Generic Kubernetes Operator Engine
meta.description: A generic, Jinja2-template-driven Kubernetes operator engine, with Secure Namespace Operator as reference implementation.

hero.title: Generic Operator
hero.tagline: A generic, Jinja2-template-driven Kubernetes operator engine — with Secure Namespace Operator as reference implementation.

problems.heading: The problem
problems.intro: Building a Kubernetes operator for on-demand provisioning — namespaces, quotas, network isolation, ingress, egress — requires a solid foundation (reconciliation loop, template rendering, revision tracking, RBAC) before writing a single line of business logic.
problems.p1_title: Duplicated code for every new need
problems.p1_text: The kopf loop, template rendering, generic resource application, and revision tracking get rewritten identically from one operator to the next.
problems.p2_text: A homegrown mutating/validating webhook means TLS certificates, cert-manager, and network availability to the API server — operational overhead for what's often simple logic.
problems.p3_text: Without a native OCI registry, publishing and versioning a Helm chart for a platform team stays manual and hard to reproduce.
problems.audience: Target audience: platform / SRE teams operating multi-tenant Kubernetes who need to expose secure, self-service namespace provisioning.

solutions.heading: The approach
solutions.before_1: Business logic and operator mechanics mixed together in the same code
solutions.before_2: A Flask webhook + cert-manager for every mutation/validation, however small
solutions.before_3: CRD group/version hardcoded throughout the Python code
solutions.after_2b: for admission — zero webhook to operate
solutions.after_3: drives the targeted CRD — group/version/kind/plural never hardcoded
solutions.ref_title: Secure Namespace Operator — the bundled reference implementation
solutions.ref_text: Secure namespace provisioning with Cilium network isolation, resource quotas, multi-controller ingress (NGINX/HAProxy/Traefik), and a VIP-based egress gateway with L2 announcement — all generated from Jinja2 templates, with no per-namespace Python code.

features.heading: Features
features.f1_text: kopf + Jinja2 rendering with custom delimiters + generic resource application via the DynamicClient.
features.f2_text: NetworkPolicies generated automatically, with configurable external-access rules (CIDR, FQDN, services, namespaces).
features.f3_text: NGINX, HAProxy, or Traefik — a dedicated controller per provisioned namespace.
features.f4_text: Automatic VIP placement with L2 announcement and Cilium policies — now unified into the generic engine.
features.f5_text: Auto-generates the name, validates required fields — replaces a homegrown mutating/validating webhook.
features.f6_text: Every spec change is tracked — revision incremented, diff and audit trail kept in a ConfigMap.
features.f7_text: Automatically published to ghcr.io via GitHub Actions on every tag — direct OCI install.
